title: Phase 2 · Build: Create, Deploy and Equip the Agent
html:
Goal: As developer, deploy Unicorn Company's customer-service agents to AgentCore with two creation methods and walk through the five-stage pipeline generate → package → provision → deploy → register. Then build a managed knowledge base from three policy documents, register and approve a reply-rules skill in the Registry, attach them to the agents, and verify grounded answers and session memory on the V3 Chat and Memory pages.

Prerequisites

  • You finished the "Roles" chapter: you checked that the release policy of workspace default is gated (preset when the organiser deployed).
  • You finished the "Define" chapter: the business needs, quality dimensions and red lines are worked out. The criteria set and golden set attach to an agent, so they are created in Part 1 of the "Evaluate" chapter; this chapter sets no criteria and migrates no endpoints.
  • Most of this chapter runs as developer (password from the organiser). Building and deploying is the developer's job, and developer holds agents.deploy. Section 5 uses a second window signed in as biz-owner to approve the skill.
  • Keep one normal browser window (developer) and one private window (biz-owner).

What this chapter produces (later chapters depend on it)

Object Name Created by Used by
Strands Agents agent (ZIP path) lab-service-assistant developer Main line through evaluation, release, observability, A/B and canary
Managed Harness agent lab-policy-advisor developer Grounded policy Q&A, comparison agent
Managed knowledge base lab-unicorn-policies developer Attached to both agents
Registry Agent skill record lab-unicorn-service-rules Registered by developer, approved by biz-owner Attached to lab-policy-advisor
(Optional) container agent or BYOC agent lab-legacy-container (section 3, option A) or lab-legacy-agent (option B) developer This chapter only

This whole chapter runs in console V3 (ConsoleUrl/v3); do not click Back to V2 in the top bar. developer starts with the everyday "Modules" list, which hides Registry and Memory. Click Show every module at the bottom of "Modules" in the left rail to see every entry. It is a view filter, not a permission: opening /v3/registry or /v3/memory directly, or searching for the page with ⌘K, works too.

0. Four creation methods, unequal capabilities

V3's New agent page (/v3/create) has the "Quick deploy · managed Harness" form on the left, and "Other ways to build" on the right lists Strands (an agent the platform generates with the Strands Agents framework), Other Agent SDK, Bring your own code and more. All four methods feed the same five-stage pipeline, but later chapters need capabilities that only some methods have:

Capability Managed Harness Strands (ZIP path) Other Agent SDK (container) Bring your own code (BYOC)
Build artifact None, declarative Platform-generated code; arm64 dependencies zipped and uploaded to S3 CodeBuild builds an ARM64 image and pushes it to ECR The zip / Dockerfile / ECR image you supply
Managed knowledge base Through the KB gateway (per-KB search + multi-step agentic retrieval) kb_search / kb_deep_search built into the generated code kb_search / kb_deep_search built into the generated code Not supported; implement it in your code
Registry skills Attached declaratively Packed into the zip Baked into the image under .claude/skills/ Not supported
Configuration-bundle A/B Not supported Supported (Config-bundle contract built in) Not supported Degraded
Model source selector Yes Yes (pinned to Bedrock for A2A) No; pinned to Bedrock + Claude Replaced by an "Allowed models" list

The main-line agent therefore uses Strands (ZIP path): the A/B experiment and the canary later require an agent that reads its system prompt through get_config_bundle(), and only the platform-generated Strands Agents code carries that contract.

1. Deploy lab-service-assistant with Strands (ZIP path)

1.1 Open the creation wizard

  1. Sign in to ConsoleUrl/v3 as developer, click Agents (/v3/agents) in the left rail, then New agent at the top right (or open "Modules" → Agent development → New agent; the address is /v3/create).
  2. Skip the scenario templates under "Start from" and the quick deploy form on the left. Under "Other ways to build" on the right, click Strands (A generated Strands agent, single agent or A2A, packaged as a zip).
  3. The creation wizard opens inside the V3 shell (/v2/agents?view=new&method=zip_runtime). The header shows three steps, Creation method → Configure → Review and deploy; Strands is preselected, so the wizard starts on Configure.

In the image: 1 Strands under "OTHER WAYS TO BUILD" (an agent the platform generates with Strands Agents, packaged as a zip); click it to open the wizard.

1.2 Fill in the configuration

Fill in the table below and leave everything else at its default:

Card · field Value
Basic information · Display name Leave empty (lists then show the resource name, which later chapters refer to)
Basic information · Resource name lab-service-assistant (cannot change after creation)
Basic information · System prompt See the code block below
Service protocol HTTP · standard invocations (default). Do not pick A2A: an A2A runtime accepts no endpoint qualifier and cannot take part in gated release
Model · Model source Keep the default Bedrock (hint: Offer models that use the Converse API.)
Model · Model Keep the default GLM-5.3 (global); the Model ID shows global.zai.glm-5.3
Tools · Template tools calculator, current_utc_time (ship with the template, nothing to tick)
Tools · Gateway tools / Demo toolkit None (do not tick hr_assistant; it replaces the template tools)
Identity, Inbound auth Defaults (Inbound auth: Inherit workspace default)
Skills and knowledge Nothing in this section; you attach them in section 6
File system Default
Memory · Long-term memory Keep Remember user preferences and facts across sessions ticked (short-term session memory is always on)
Memory · Memory resource Keep Platform default (shared workspace memory)

System prompt. It is deliberately ordinary: the A/B chapter analyzes it and proposes an improved version, and a polished prompt here would leave nothing to compare.

text
You are the customer service assistant of Unicorn Company, serving users of two business lines: Unicorn Mall (online shopping) and Unicorn Trip (flights and hotels). Answer questions about products, orders, returns and exchanges, flight changes and refunds, baggage, and hotel booking cancellations in a friendly, concise way.

Keep both the model source and the model at their defaults: GLM-5.3 (global) is the first entry of the Bedrock list, its global inference profile answers in both us-east-1 and us-west-2, and when the organiser deployed the environment the template probed global.zai.glm-5.3 with a real Converse call.

In the image: 1 Resource name lab-service-assistant; 2 System prompt; 3 Service protocol stays HTTP · standard invocations; 4 Model source Bedrock; 5 Model GLM-5.3 (global), with Model ID global.zai.glm-5.3 next to it; 6 the Config-bundle contract note at the bottom of the Memory card.

The note under the Memory card says two things: the generated agent has the Config-bundle contract built in (get_config_bundle() reads the system prompt and tool descriptions, with defaults as fallback), and OTEL (ADOT) instrumentation is added automatically. The evaluation, A/B and observability chapters rely on both.

1.3 Review and deploy

  1. Click Next to reach Review and deploy. The Review card says: Deploying installs dependencies for arm64, packages a zip and creates an AgentCore Runtime with its execution role. Check the resource name, model and memory (Short-term + long-term).
  2. Click Create and deploy.

Expected result: in under a second the agent's management page opens (/v2/agents?view=detail&id=<ID>, still inside the V3 shell; it is also what the Manage button on the V3 agent page opens) with status DEPLOYING, and the "Deployment" card shows the UI text Installing dependencies and packaging — 1 to 3 minutes and Elapsed …. In this run the whole pipeline took 53 seconds.

Meanwhile lab-service-assistant is already listed under Agents (/v3/agents) in the left rail. Click it to open the V3 agent page (/v3/agents?id=<ID>): the first "Lifecycle" node, Built, shows building…, Serving shows v— · DEFAULT, and the "Last deploy" table lists the five stages with their state (measured 7 seconds into the deploy: generate Completed, package In progress, the other three Pending); the page refreshes itself until the deploy finishes.

1.4 The five-stage pipeline

On the management page, expand Technical log in the "Deployment" card to see the five stages and the deploy log (the V3 agent page's "Last deploy" table shows only each stage's name and summary; the full log is on the management page). Every creation method runs this same pipeline (backend/app/deployer/pipeline.py); every stage is idempotent, so a restarted backend resumes at the first unfinished stage:

Stage What the Strands (ZIP) path does What to look for in the log
GENERATE Renders main.py from the Strands Agents code template with the prompt, model and memory settings strands template · 28810 bytes · model global.zai.glm-5.3
PACKAGE Locks and installs dependencies for linux/aarch64, zips them and uploads to the artifacts bucket requirements locked · 112 packages pinned with hashes, pip+zip 18.7s · 38.3MB → s3://…/agents/lab-service-assistant/deployment_package.zip
PROVISION Creates an IAM execution role for this agent alone created execution role launchpad-agent-lab-service-assistant-<first 8 characters of the agent ID>
DEPLOY CreateAgentRuntime, then polls until READY execution-role permissions not yet visible (IAM propagation) — retry 1/5 in 10s (the new role needs IAM propagation; the retry after 10 seconds is normal), CreateAgentRuntime accepted · runtimeId lab_service_assistant_…, runtime status: CREATING, runtime status: READY
REGISTER Creates an A2A record in AgentCore Registry and submits it for approval a2a record created · <RECORD_ID> · auto-submitted

In the image: 1 expand "Technical log"; 2 all five stages GENERATE, PACKAGE, PROVISION, DEPLOY, REGISTER are Done, with the deploy log below; 3 the V3 agent page's "LIFECYCLE": CANDIDATE and GATE show not gated, SERVING shows v1 · DEFAULT; 4 "LAST DEPLOY" lists each stage's summary.

Expected result: all five stages show Done, the status turns ACTIVE, and "Deployment" shows Ready in 53s (measured in this run: generate under 1 s, package 20 s, provision under 1 s, deploy 31 s including the 10-second IAM propagation retry, register 3 s). In the management page's "Basic information", the ARN looks like arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:<account>:runtime/lab_service_assistant_<6-character random suffix>-… and "Registry record" has a value.

1.5 Where does a first deploy land in a gated workspace?

The workspace is gated, yet this deploy does not land on a candidate endpoint and opens no pending release record. The reason is the bookkeeping after a successful deploy (_finish in pipeline.py → after_deploy in app/dlc/releases.py):

  • Every new agent starts with endpoint_mode = default: production traffic uses the auto-rolling AgentCore DEFAULT endpoint.
  • after_deploy only acts on agents that were migrated to named endpoints (endpoint_mode = live). For an unmigrated agent it returns immediately, whether the workspace is direct or gated.
  • Migration (creating a live endpoint at the current version and moving traffic onto it) is done by release-ops, who holds release.sign, in Part 3 of the "Evaluate" chapter. Only after that does each redeploy by developer update candidate alone, with live moving when a release is signed.

So in this chapter every deploy and redeploy of lab-service-assistant and lab-policy-advisor takes effect immediately, and the Chat page uses the new version right away. The V3 agent page (/v3/agents?id=<ID>) confirms it: in "Lifecycle" the Candidate and Gate nodes both show not gated and Serving shows v1 · DEFAULT; the "Versions" table's "Serving on" column has only DEFAULT.

Do not call the migration API yourself in this chapter. Migration needs release.sign, which is release-ops's duty; Part 3 of the "Evaluate" chapter walks through it.

1.6 Ask a question it cannot answer without the knowledge base

In the "Try it" card at the bottom of the V3 agent page, type the question below and click Run:

text
I bought a Unicorn Air Standard fare ticket. The fare is ¥1,200 and I'm cancelling 3 days before departure. How much do I get back?

Note the answer. The agent has no policy material yet, so the answer can only come from the model's own impression. This chapter asked it once on each of three fresh lab-service-assistant deployments (in Chinese), and all three answers were wrong. The most recent observed answer ("Try it" showed 12s), translated:

Under Unicorn Air's Standard fare rules, a refund requested more than 48 hours before departure (3 days counts) carries a fee of 10% of the fare. … Refund fee: 1200 × 10% = ¥120; expected refund: 1200 − 120 = ¥1,080 …

The correct answer (from the policy documents in section 4) is: fee 25% = ¥300, so ¥900 of fare plus ¥80 of taxes, ¥980 in total. You ask again in section 7 after attaching the knowledge base.

2. Create lab-policy-advisor with managed Harness

A Harness is declarative: you give the model, prompt, tools, skills, knowledge bases and memory switches, and AgentCore hosts it directly. There is no build artifact.

  1. Go back to New agent (/v3/create). "Start from" has Start from scratch selected by default, and the "Quick deploy · managed Harness" form on the left only has the name, instructions and knowledge. This lab sets the model and turns off native execution, so do not deploy from here: click Full form at the top right of that card.

  2. The wizard opens inside the V3 shell (/v2/agents?view=new&scenario=blank) with the managed Harness method, straight on the full form of the Configure step.

  3. Fill in:

    Card · field Value
    Basic information · Resource name lab-policy-advisor (leave Display name empty)
    Basic information · System prompt See the code block below
    Model · Model source / Model Keep the defaults Bedrock / GLM-5.3 (global) (global.zai.glm-5.3)
    Model · Max output tokens per call, Reasoning effort Defaults
    Tools · Built-in tools, Gateway tools, Remote MCP servers None
    Tools · Native execution Untick Shell and File operations. Policy Q&A never needs to run commands, and every capability removed is one less way to overstep
    Skills and knowledge Nothing in this section; you attach them in section 6
    Memory and loop · Long-term memory Tick Remember user preferences and facts across sessions (it starts unticked when you come from "Start from scratch")
    Memory and loop · the rest Defaults: platform default memory, default iterations and timeout
    PII protection · Mode Keep Off
    text
    You are Unicorn Company's policy advisor. Answer only from the attached policy knowledge base, covering Unicorn Mall returns and refunds, Unicorn Air flight changes, refunds and baggage, and Unicorn Hotels cancellations and changes. Cite the clause number you rely on; show the calculation whenever a fee is involved; if the knowledge base does not cover something, say clearly that you cannot confirm it and do not guess.

  4. Click Next → check the Review (Deploying creates an AgentCore Harness and its execution role) → Create and deploy.

Expected result: in this run the status was ACTIVE after 28 seconds. The technical log (<…> marks random values that differ for everyone):

text
generate   harness request generated for lab_policy_advisor · model global.zai.glm-5.3 (bedrock · converse_stream)
package    skipped · harness — no build required
provision  created execution role launchpad-agent-lab-policy-advisor-<first 8 characters of the agent ID>
deploy     execution-role permissions not yet visible (IAM propagation) — retry 1/5 in 10s
deploy     CreateHarness accepted · harnessId lab_policy_advisor-<10-character random suffix>
deploy     harness READY · arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:<account>:harness/lab_policy_advisor-<10-character random suffix>
register   a2a record created · <RECORD_ID> · auto-submitted

The PACKAGE stage shows Skipped: a Harness has no build artifact. The ARN contains :harness/, not :runtime/.

Two Harness constraints matter later:

  • A Harness does run on a managed Runtime, but you cannot invoke that Runtime directly, only through the Harness invoke API; configuration-bundle A/B has no effect on a Harness.
  • A Harness's log group exists only after its first invocation. Before the evaluation chapter evaluates it, you must have chatted with it at least once in section 7.

3. (Optional) Migrate an existing agent: container or BYOC

This section shows two ways to bring existing agent code across. Pick either one, or skip it; later chapters do not depend on it. Option A deploys lab-legacy-container with the Claude Agent SDK container and is the only path that uses a Claude model; option B deploys lab-legacy-agent. The names differ, so doing both causes no clash. option B is a complete LangChain → Strands Agents migration with two tools the agent really calls, and is the one we recommend.

Option A: Other Agent SDK (Claude Agent SDK container)

  1. New agent (/v3/create) → click Other Agent SDK under "Other ways to build"; the wizard starts on Configure.

  2. Fill in:

    Card · field Value
    Basic information · Resource name lab-legacy-container
    Basic information · System prompt You are Unicorn Trip's itinerary assistant. Given the user's origin, destination and dates, suggest flight and hotel bookings.
    Agent SDK Claude Agent SDK (selected by default; the note says It is the only SDK in this category today.)
    Model Keep the default Claude Sonnet 5 (global) (global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5); the model source is pinned to Bedrock, with the hint The Claude Agent SDK can only drive Claude models, so the model source is pinned to Bedrock.
    SDK capabilities, Skills and knowledge, File system, Memory Defaults

    The bottom of the Memory card shows the same Config-bundle contract baked in. … note, but the Claude Agent SDK code template (backend/app/templates/claude_sdk_agent/) contains no get_config_bundle(); for configuration-bundle A/B go by the table in section 0: the container method does not support it.

  3. Next → the Review card says Deploying builds an ARM64 container image in CodeBuild, pushes it to ECR and creates an AgentCore Runtime. and "Model" is global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 → Create and deploy.

Expected result: all five stages turn Done and the whole pipeline takes about 2 minutes (measured 2 min 00 s in total: generate under 1 s; package 96 s, of which CodeBuild 80 s followed by a 16 s wait at the scan gate for the ECR image scan; provision under 1 s; deploy 21 s, including a 10 s IAM propagation retry; register 3 s). The PACKAGE summary is codebuild · arm64 · 1.3m → :lab-legacy-container-v1 @ sha256:…. The GENERATE log reads build context assembled: Dockerfile, README.md, buildspec.yml, main.py, requirements.txt, summary container context · 5 files; the PACKAGE log shows, in order, source zip uploaded → s3://…/builds/lab-legacy-container/source.zip, codebuild started · launchpad-agent-builder:…, codebuild phase: QUEUED → PRE_BUILD → BUILD → POST_BUILD → COMPLETED, image pushed · …/launchpad-agents:lab-legacy-container-v1 · sha256:…, then the scan gate: image scan: IN_PROGRESS right after the push, the gate waits for the result, image scan: COMPLETE 16 s later, and then it reads image scan findings · HIGH 8, MEDIUM 3, LOW 2: no CRITICAL, so the gate lets the image through. PROVISION shows created execution role launchpad-agent-lab-legacy-container-…; DEPLOY shows execution-role permissions not yet visible (IAM propagation) — retry 1/5 in 10s, CreateAgentRuntime accepted · runtimeId lab_legacy_container_… · inbound auth iam, then runtime status: CREATING → READY; REGISTER shows a2a record created · … · auto-submitted and registry (A2A) created · …. "Deploy progress" on the manage page reads Ready in …, and the V3 agent page shows CONTAINER above the title.

Five green stages only prove the image was pushed and the Runtime is READY, not that the container process starts. Check it once after the deploy: click Agents in the rail → the lab-legacy-container row, type the sentence below into the "Try it" card at the bottom of the agent page, and click Run:

text
I'm going from Shanghai to Chengdu next week. Recommend flights and a hotel for me.

Expected result: a normal reply comes back and the card shows the latency (18s in this run). One observed answer (sent in Chinese, excerpt translated):

Sure! To recommend Shanghai → Chengdu flights and hotels precisely I need a few more details: Flights: your exact departure date … Shanghai has two airports, Hongqiao (SHA) and Pudong (PVG) … Chengdu also has Tianfu (TFU) and Shuangliu (CTU) … Hotel: how many nights … which part of Chengdu you want to stay in; common choices: Chunxi Road / Taikoo Li … Kuanzhai Alley / Qintai Road … near the Giant Panda Base … around Tianfu Square … General advice: booking 7–10 days ahead keeps fares steadier … Tell me your dates and budget and I can narrow it down further.

If it returns RuntimeClientError instead, the container process did not start; see Troubleshooting in this chapter.

This agent exists only for this demo. Once it has answered you can delete it as in section 2.4 of the "Wrap-up and cleanup" chapter: Agents → lab-legacy-container → Manage → Delete, then Delete in the Delete agent dialog (Delete lab-legacy-container and its AgentCore resources? This cannot be undone.).

Option B: Bring your own code (BYOC) — migrate a LangChain agent to Strands Agents, then ship it

This section is a complete migration: the team already has a tool-calling agent written with LangChain, moves it to the Strands Agents framework, and deploys it to AgentCore with BYOC. It all happens in the browser; no AWS or IAM permissions are needed anywhere in the flow.

The sample comes from the Launchpad repository's samples/byoc/langchain-to-strands/ and is packaged for you; download it:

  • lab-legacy-agent.zip: the zip you upload and deploy, holding exactly three files, main.py, policy_tools.py and requirements.txt.
  • langchain-to-strands-source.zip: the full sample (including the before state legacy_langchain/ and the README.md), for reading and comparing only; you do not upload it.

The files of the sample:

File Role
policy_tools.py Two tools: refund_quote (change/refund fee from fare, fare family and hours to departure) and baggage_allowance (allowance and excess fees). The numbers come from this workshop's policy rules A-02–A-15. Not a single line of this file changes in the migration.
legacy_langchain/main.py Before: LangChain's create_agent + ChatBedrockConverse, served from a hand-written FastAPI route POST /chat
main.py After: Strands Agents' Agent + BedrockModel, with BedrockAgentCoreApp providing the POST /invocations and GET /ping that BYOC requires

B.1 The four things that change

The runtime contract is ARM64 · port 8080 · POST /invocations + GET /ping, with the payload {"prompt": "...", "actor_id": "..."}. Compare the two files and only four things differ:

# What changes Before (LangChain) After (Strands Agents)
1 Tool decorator from langchain_core.tools import tool from strands import Agent, tool
2 Model object ChatBedrockConverse(model=MODEL_ID) BedrockModel(model_id=MODEL_ID)
3 Construction and call create_agent(...), invoked with a message list, answered with content blocks Agent(...), called with the question; str(result) is the text
4 The outside interface A hand-written FastAPI route BedrockAgentCoreApp + @app.entrypoint, with the entrypoint streaming delta / tool / complete events

Both frameworks read the tool description from the docstring and build the parameter schema from the type hints, so the two lines that wrap the tools are identical in both versions:

python
refund_tool = tool(refund_quote)
baggage_tool = tool(baggage_allowance)

That is also why policy_tools.py needs no edits: the business logic is framework-independent, and the migration only replaces the shell around it.

Here are both main.py files in full; read them against the four rows above.

After: main.py (the one inside lab-legacy-agent.zip)

python
"""AFTER — the same agent on Strands Agents, deployable as Launchpad BYOC.

Four things changed from `legacy_langchain/main.py`; the tools in
`policy_tools.py` did not change at all:

1. the tool decorator: `langchain_core.tools.tool` -> `strands.tool`
2. the model object: `ChatBedrockConverse(model=...)` -> `BedrockModel(model_id=...)`
3. the agent call: `create_agent(...).invoke({"messages": [...]})` -> `Agent(...)(prompt)`
4. the server: a FastAPI route -> `BedrockAgentCoreApp` + `@app.entrypoint`,
   which is what gives Launchpad `POST /invocations` and `GET /ping` on :8080;
   the entrypoint streams `delta` / `tool` / `complete` events so the console
   shows each tool call next to the answer

`MODEL_ID` is injected by Launchpad: it is the first entry of the wizard's
**Allowed models** list, and the execution role may invoke only that list.
"""

import os
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Any

from bedrock_agentcore.runtime import BedrockAgentCoreApp
from strands import Agent, tool
from strands.models import BedrockModel

# isort: split
# the sample's own module, shared with legacy_langchain/main.py
from policy_tools import SYSTEM_PROMPT, baggage_allowance, refund_quote

MODEL_ID = os.environ.get("MODEL_ID", "global.zai.glm-5.3")

# Identical to the LangChain version: both frameworks read the description from
# the docstring and the schema from the type hints.
refund_tool = tool(refund_quote)
baggage_tool = tool(baggage_allowance)

app = BedrockAgentCoreApp()


def build_agent() -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=BedrockModel(model_id=MODEL_ID),
        tools=[refund_tool, baggage_tool],
        system_prompt=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        # the default handler prints every token to stdout; the stream below
        # already carries them to the console, so keep the runtime log clean
        callback_handler=None,
    )


@app.entrypoint
async def invoke(payload: dict) -> AsyncIterator[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Launchpad sends {"prompt": "...", "actor_id": "..."}.

    The reply is streamed in the platform's runtime envelope, the same one the
    platform-generated Strands agents use: `delta` for text as it arrives, one
    `tool` per tool call (so the console shows which tool ran), and `complete`
    with the final answer. A plain `{"result": "..."}` would work too, but the
    console could then show the answer only, not the tool calls behind it.
    """
    prompt = str(payload.get("prompt", "")).strip()
    if not prompt:
        yield {"event": "error", "message": "payload must include a non-empty 'prompt'"}
        return
    # A fresh Agent per request keeps turns isolated: Launchpad passes the actor
    # and session itself, and this sample holds no conversation state.
    seen: set[str] = set()
    result: Any = None
    try:
        async for event in build_agent().stream_async(prompt):
            if not isinstance(event, dict):
                continue
            text = event.get("data")
            if isinstance(text, str) and text:
                yield {"event": "delta", "text": text}
            tool_use = event.get("current_tool_use")
            if isinstance(tool_use, dict) and tool_use.get("name"):
                key = str(tool_use.get("toolUseId") or tool_use["name"])
                if key not in seen:
                    seen.add(key)
                    yield {
                        "event": "tool",
                        "name": str(tool_use["name"]),
                        "id": tool_use.get("toolUseId"),
                    }
            if "result" in event:
                result = event["result"]
    except Exception as exc:  # surfaced as a failed turn in the console
        yield {"event": "error", "message": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
        return
    yield {"event": "complete", "result": str(result) if result is not None else ""}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

Before: legacy_langchain/main.py (only in langchain-to-strands-source.zip, never deployed)

python
"""BEFORE — the agent the team already had, written with LangChain.

This file is here to be migrated, not to be deployed: it serves its own FastAPI
app on whatever path the team picked, so it does not satisfy the Launchpad BYOC
contract (`POST /invocations` + `GET /ping` on :8080). Run it locally to see what
the agent did before the move:

    pip install -r requirements.txt
    uvicorn main:app --port 8000
    curl -s localhost:8000/chat -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"question": "标准经济舱 1200 元，起飞前 3 天退票能退多少？"}'

The migrated version lives one directory up (`../main.py`): same tools, same
prompt, Strands instead of LangChain, and the AgentCore entrypoint Launchpad
expects.
"""

import os
import sys

from fastapi import FastAPI
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_aws import ChatBedrockConverse
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from pydantic import BaseModel

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from policy_tools import SYSTEM_PROMPT, baggage_allowance, refund_quote  # noqa: E402

MODEL_ID = os.environ.get("MODEL_ID", "global.zai.glm-5.3")

# Both frameworks read the description from the docstring and the schema from
# the type hints, so these two lines are identical in the migrated version —
# only the `tool` import above differs.
refund_tool = tool(refund_quote)
baggage_tool = tool(baggage_allowance)

agent = create_agent(
    model=ChatBedrockConverse(model=MODEL_ID),
    tools=[refund_tool, baggage_tool],
    system_prompt=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
)

app = FastAPI()


class Ask(BaseModel):
    question: str


def _text(content: str | list) -> str:
    """ChatBedrockConverse returns a list of content blocks, not a plain string."""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    return "".join(b.get("text", "") for b in content if isinstance(b, dict))


@app.post("/chat")
def chat(ask: Ask) -> dict[str, str]:
    result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": ask.question}]})
    return {"answer": _text(result["messages"][-1].content)}

MODEL_ID is injected by the platform as the first entry of the Allowed models list, and the execution role may invoke only the models in that list. So never hard-code a model id — read it from the environment.

Above each answer there is a tool-call line with a wrench icon: refund_quote for the refund question, baggage_allowance for the baggage one (the tool name is the function name, so it reads the same in both UI languages). The tool lines show up because the sample's entrypoint streams its reply: text as delta, one tool event per tool call, then complete, the same envelope the platform-generated Strands Agents code uses; an entrypoint that returned only {"result": ...} would show the answer alone. Try it at the bottom of the agent page shows only the raw final answer (Markdown is not rendered) and the latency, without tool lines, so use Chat to check the tools.

If the reply turns into a single line RuntimeError: EventStreamError: … internalServerException …, the model side had a transient error that the sample reported as an error event; click New conversation and send the question again.

The system prompt states that any amount must come from a tool rather than an estimate. When the numbers in the answer do not match, look for the tool line above it: no tool line means the model skipped the tool and answered from its own impression — the same class of error as in section 1.6 with no knowledge base attached.

A BYOC agent cannot mount tools, skills or a knowledge base from the form; all of that lives in your own code — the two tools in this sample are an example of exactly that.

5. Register and approve the skill lab-unicorn-service-rules

The Registry is the discovery layer: it catalogs A2A agents, MCP tools and agent skills, and gates their visibility with Draft → Pending approval → Published. Only Published (APPROVED) records can be attached to agents. This skill turns the customer-service reply rules (cite clauses, show calculations, mask personal data, never overpromise) into a reusable asset.

5.1 developer registers and submits

  1. As developer, open "Modules" → Agent development → Registry (/v3/registry). The "Waiting on approval" card (and the Waiting approval figure at the top) shows the A2A records the deploys created automatically: one each from sections 1 and 2, plus lab-legacy-agent if you did option B in section 3 (3 records in this run).
  2. Click Register at the top right; the register form opens inside the V3 shell (/v2/registry?view=register). Under "Record type" choose Agent skill; under "Source" choose Paste SKILL.md.
  3. "Basic information" card:
    • Name: lab-unicorn-service-rules
    • Description: Unicorn Company customer-service reply rules: cite clause numbers, show fee calculations, mask personal data, never promise refunds or ticketing beyond policy.
    • SKILL.md content:
markdown
---
name: lab-unicorn-service-rules
description: Unicorn Company customer-service reply rules. Use when answering about returns, refunds, flight changes or refunds, baggage, hotel cancellations or fee calculations, or when the conversation contains a phone number, ID number or other personal data.
---

# Unicorn Company customer-service reply rules

1. Lead with the conclusion, then the basis: cite the policy clause number, e.g. (per A-03).
2. Whenever an amount is involved, show the calculation, e.g. 1200 × 25% = 300; refund 1200 − 300 + 80 = ¥980.
3. Always mask personal data before writing it, even if the user supplied the full number:
   - phone numbers show only the first 3 and last 4 digits, e.g. 138****5678;
   - ID document numbers show only the first 4 and last 4 characters, with * in between.
4. Never promise a refund, free change, ticket issuance or compensation the policy does not allow. When a request exceeds the policy, explain why and offer a transfer to a human agent.
5. If the policy does not cover something, say "the policy does not specify this"; never guess a number.

8.1 Let the agent remember preferences

Based on your usual preferences (aisle seat on flights, high-floor king room in hotels), here are a few tips (translated). (Optional) The container agent's PACKAGE stage fails with image scan findings · CRITICAL … and RuntimeError: image launchpad-agents@sha256:… has blocking vulnerabilities (CRITICAL …) at or above CRITICAL — CVE-… After pushing the image the platform scans it in ECR and blocks the deploy on any CRITICAL finding. The image is rebuilt on every deploy from the Debian base image of the Claude Agent SDK template, so a newly published CRITICAL vulnerability in that base image gets it blocked; nothing in the form can fix it, and the image_scan_block_severities / image_scan_enabled settings the error mentions are the organiser's platform configuration Tell the organiser and send them the CVE id and package from the error (the platform's container template needs an update). Retry in the "Versions" card of the V3 agent page only reloads the versions list and does not redeploy; until the organiser updates the template, a redeploy builds the same image and is blocked again. Once it is updated, delete the failed agent as in the last paragraph of section 3 option A and create it again per option A (the generate stage uses the updated template). Option A is optional, so you can do option B instead; later chapters are unaffected
(Optional) The container agent deployed but invoking it fails with RuntimeClientError The container process did not start Check that Runtime's log group in CloudWatch; skipping this path does not affect later chapters
